rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so this candidate shifts moderately toward stronger obfuscation. SUB and SPLIT carry low real-world cost and risk, so their Security/Diversity weights stay high to ensure broad application across the 13 small functions; their Runtime/Size weights are kept low so hot or compact functions are not excluded. BCF and FLA provide the bulk of control-flow resistance: BCF gets high security/diversity with a moderate SizeCost weight since the reference text is only ~1.5 KB and absorbing some growth is acceptable, while FLA targets the larger recursive functions (Towers, Move, tower) with a slightly higher RuntimeCost weight and an elevated CorrectnessRisk weight so the selector avoids flattening fragile recursive or exception-like CFGs where it could alter behavior. IBR and ICALL add dynamic-analysis friction but cost indirect dispatch at runtime, so their RuntimeCost weights are kept near the middle to concentrate them on non-hot functions like Init, Push, and Puzzle setup. IGV remains enabled at moderate weights to obscure global state access cheaply. Overall, cheap structural passes dominate while expensive dispatch-transformations are gated by runtime sensitivity, preserving correctness (risk weights all <= 0.25) after a clean round-0 run.
